item.text:
<linkedin_post>Speaker attribution can be as important as the words in a transcript. A meeting record that assigns a decision to the wrong person may be misleading even when the sentence itself is accurate.

NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe uses speaker cues alongside audio features to label turns as it generates a transcript. On David AI’s diarization benchmark across 21 languages, it recorded an 18.26% diarization error rate, the lowest among the 14 systems tested. It also led VoiceArena’s English full-session benchmark, which includes overlapping speech and recordings with two to eight speakers.

The error rates are a reminder to check speaker changes against the recording, particularly when a transcript will be used to document decisions or attribute statements. The model is built for recorded audio, so it won’t provide live speaker labels during a meeting.</linkedin_post>
